structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E016.

The setup
- The tip is E016: the E015 recipe (Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, CUDA graphs, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs ≈ 238 steps, widths 128/384/512) with weight decay halved to 0.006.
- It scores 6.580 s and 0.7607.

Why I discount E016's gain
- Muon renormalizes the filters to a fixed norm and has no weight-decay term. So weight decay touches only the BatchNorm biases, the whitening bias and the head.
- The +0.33 pp is therefore mostly a reshuffle of the 3-seed mean, about ±0.25 pp per path change, plus perhaps 0.1 pp of real effect.
- The tip's true mean is about 0.758 ± 0.2.

Time model
- Training is GPU-bound. The cost of a step scales roughly with pixel count and with batch size.
- There is a fixed host cost of about 0.35 s.
- Small resolutions use the GPU somewhat less efficiently, so the savings are below linear.

Where the FLOPs are (per-image conv FLOPs at 32 px)
- Group 1: about 20%.
- Group 2: about 50%.
- Group 3: about 28%.
- Narrowing group 2 also cheapens group 3's first conv.

Exchange rates for accuracy against time
- Epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% of time.
- Width: about 0.5-0.9 pp per 10%.
- Moderate resizing: about 0.3 pp per 10%. A 20 px stage is a cliff.

Accuracy mechanisms
- Accuracy is set mainly late in training, by endpoint averaging (EMA/Lookahead) at a low LR and at 32 px.
- Early low-resolution epochs mostly do coarse feature learning, which can be bought cheaply. But removing them still costs something, because the LR peak happens there.

Batch size
- Smaller batches give more Muon steps, which plausibly helps accuracy.
- The cost is a fixed Newton-Schulz overhead per step and lower GPU efficiency at the smaller batch.

forecasts.reason: Moving 30% of steps from 28 to 24 px cuts pixel-work about 8% (≈0.35 s after efficiency losses). The cost is roughly 0.3 pp, which is about the same exchange rate as cutting epochs, so it is not clearly better than a uniform trim.
Cutting 19 cheap 24 px steps saves about 5%. The 32 px tail stays the same length, so the loss is about 0.2-0.3 pp. That fits a smooth epoch dial.
E012 showed that rebuilding with max-autotune gives bit-identical results. Held-out seeds will probably sit about 0.2-0.3 pp below 0.7607.

There are 60% more Muon steps, which plausibly adds +0.2-0.5 pp. But the extra Newton-Schulz calls and the lower efficiency at the smaller batch cost about 6-8% of time, so it only pays off if the gain is later spent on epochs.
Scalar optimizer retunes have been flat (E009/E013/E014). A momentum change mostly reshuffles the 3-seed mean around the tip's true value of about 0.758.
This cuts about 16% of conv FLOPs, or about 7% of wall time. The width exchange rate predicts a loss of about 0.4-0.6 pp, which could land near the bar.

cruxes: What is E016's mean on held-out seeds 3-12? If it is about 0.758 rather than 0.7607, only about 0.5 epoch of margin can be spent, not about 1 epoch.
Is accuracy set mainly in the final 32 px, low-LR phase? If so, cutting 24 px steps (I023/I024) beats a uniform epoch trim; if not, all FLOP cuts trade at the same rate.
Does a smaller batch (more Muon steps) buy enough accuracy per unit of time to fund an epoch cut that more than offsets its 6-8% step-time overhead?
